input.standard: ASTM E741 (concentration decay, single zone); ASTM D6245 (occupant CO2 as tracer)
input.purpose: Measure V_lab, the volume of air served by /habitat/lab/eclss/scrubber-1-t7, as V = Qe * tau from a raise-then-decay CO2 curve with the two Lab occupants as the source.

steps.why: Rise: scrubber effective flow cut to 0.4 m3/min so the Lab CO2 climbs from 1000 ppm toward a higher equilibrium (~1900 ppm for 2 awake occupants), several hundred ppm above sensor noise.
Decay: full speed (Qe 1 m3/min), record the fall toward its equilibrium (~760 ppm, expected tau = V/Qe ~ 30 min for a first guess V = 30 m3); fit C(t)=Ceq+(C0-Ceq)exp(-t/tau).

abort.when: the device refuses a step's command
a monitored person out of band 45-120 bpm, monitoring lost, or one more person enters the Lab

monitoring.reason: The two Lab occupants breathe the raised CO2 during the rise; Hab-B occupants are outside the volume under test.

expected.rise: Lab CO2 rises from ~1000 ppm by roughly 250-300 ppm over 28 min (first guess V=30 m3, tau_rise ~ 75 min at 40 percent, plus 3.33 min scrubber lag); peak well under 2500 ppm.
expected.decay: After returning to 100 percent, CO2 falls toward ~760 ppm (G/Qe = 0.76 L/min / 1000 L/min) with tau ~ 30 min if V=30 m3; fitted tau times Qe=1 m3/min gives V_lab, expected inside the 10-200 m3 range, near 30 m3.
expected.hypothesis_failure: A fitted equilibrium far from ~760 ppm, a residual not flat, a rise in Hab-B CO2 while the Lab falls, or a tau inconsistent between phases shows the hatch leaks (exchange not zero) or the Lab is not well mixed, and V_lab is then an upper/biased estimate.
expected.commands: Every speed command is accepted by the device; a refusal aborts.

hypotheses: The Lab is one well-mixed zone (single-zone assumption).

The closed hatch to Hab-B is held closed throughout; exchange through it is not measured and not assumed zero (station-topology design flow 3 m3/min with hatch closed); Hab-B CO2 is recorded to reveal it.
Occupants stay 2 and at constant awake activity (0.38 L/min each) during the test; nobody enters or leaves.
Scrubber effective flow is the datasheet value, Qe = c x 1.0 m3/min, with first-order lag 3.33 min; the lag is accounted for by fitting after ~3.33 min of each step change.
The first guess V=30 m3 is only used to size durations, not as a result.
Records: Lab CO2 every minute, Hab-B CO2 every minute, scrubber speed commands and acceptance.
